glosses: To revolve or rotate around a centre.

examples.text: The body was turning round slowly as it fell.

glosses: To turn so as to be facing in the opposite direction.

examples.text: It seemed that there was someone behind me; but when I turned round, no one was there.

examples.text: You can't turn round and blame me all of a sudden.

examples.text: He turned the glass round and examined the other side.

glosses: To make (a ship, airplane etc.) ready for departure.

examples.text: The stopover is very short, and crews will have about 15 minutes to turn the plane round.

examples.text: He rotated in his chair to face me.

glosses: To advance through a sequence; to take turns.

examples.text: The nurses' shifts rotate each week.

glosses: To lift the nose during takeoff, just prior to liftoff.

examples.text: The aircraft rotates at sixty knots.

glosses: To spin, turn, or revolve something.

glosses: To advance something through a sequence; to allocate or deploy in turns.

examples.text: I've always admired the Japanese point of view that holds it best not to have a great number of objects around at one time but to rotate possessions — and display them with great simplicity.

glosses: To replace older materials or to place older materials in front of newer ones so that older ones get used first.

examples.text: The supermarket rotates the stock daily so that old foods don't sit around.
